subject: OrbitPay discovery — function-call & structured-output acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@orbitpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Malik <priya.malik@orbitpay.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: OrbitPay — demo request

Hi Monica,

Quick intro — I’m Alex, head of payments product at OrbitPay. We’re evaluating options for integrating an inference layer that can run deterministic, structured outputs for payment orchestration (e.g., route decisions, cost estimates, routing reasons).

High-level pain:
- We currently have a homegrown rules engine that is brittle and hard to maintain across partners.
- Non-deterministic LLM output in PoCs caused downstream reconciliation issues (parsers failing).

Goals for a solution:
- Deterministic, schema-backed responses for actions (JSON) that can be validated server-side.
- Tool/function calling support to integrate with our routing/quote services.
- Clear SLOs: 99th pct latency under 350ms for single-token decisions; predictable cost at scale.

Can we schedule a 30–40 min call tomorrow to walk through constraints and sample prompts? Priya (CC) will join from product.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Jordan
Head of Product — Payments
OrbitPay

2) Example prompts and expected structured outputs (JSON schema)

See you tomorrow — Monica

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@orbitpay.com>
Cc: Priya Malik <priya.malik@orbitpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitPay discovery — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the call earlier. Below is a concise recap so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of what we heard (pain / constraints):
- Primary pain: brittle business rules and manual overrides causing inconsistent routing and frequent reconciliations.
- Core requirement: deterministic, schema-validated outputs for every decision so downstream services can assert invariants (no free-text fallbacks).
- Latency SLO: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 220ms, target P99 < 350ms for typical single-decision requests at expected QPS (peak 250 rps).
- Supported call pattern: prefer REST with JSON request/response; mutual TLS for private deployments is a hard requirement for production.
- Data residency: US only for payments data (for now).

Current stack / integration points we learned:
- Front-end services publish a DecisionRequest to our routing API, which currently returns a RouteDecision JSON from the rules engine.
- We need a drop-in inference endpoint that returns validated RouteDecision objects and can optionally call back to your internal quote service for cost estimates.

Success criteria (what OrbitPay will consider a win):
- Determinism: >= 99.5% schema-conformant responses on our standard prompt set (no parser exceptions).
- Latency: P95 under 250ms for the most common path at baseline QPS.
- Integration: Able to call a function/endpoint to fetch on-demand price ticks during generation with no visible latency spike (>20% increase).
- Observability: per-request token costs + per-route latency metrics available in Redwood Console or pushed to OrbitPay’s Datadog.

Function-calling & structured output specifics discussed:
- Expected output type: RouteDecision JSON with fields: route_id, provider, estimated_cost_cents, confidence (0-1), reason_codes (array), trace_id.
- Determinism approach: schema enforcement at model boundary + deterministic formatting tests in CI using our prompt set. We discussed offering a small wrapper that validates and re-prompts on schema mismatch for a fixed retry budget.
- Tooling: prefer a function-call that can be invoked from the model to ask for live pricing: getQuote(provider, route_payload) -> {estimated_cost_cents, estimated_latency_ms}. We discussed synchronous function calls and a fallback to cached quotes.

Attachments we referenced (stubs):
- OrbitPay_PromptSet.xlsx (sample prompts and expected JSON outputs)
- OrbitPay_Security_QS.pdf (short answers to our security questionnaire)

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan):
1) OrbitPay: send 2–3 representative prompts + an exported CSV of parser failures from recent runs (Alex / Priya) — due EOD tomorrow.
2) Redwood (Monica + Marissa): produce a short proof-of-concept plan (POC) that covers: endpoint contract (schema), function-call handshake for getQuote, retry budget, and basic observability dashboard — target delivery: 3 business days.
3) If POC looks good, move to a 2-week sandbox with dedicated capacity for load testing and quantization profile assessment.

Please confirm steps and whether the timeline above works. I’ll kick off the POC doc and include a technical appendix for function-call examples.

Thanks,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | monica_patel@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: OrbitPay_PromptSet.xlsx (spreadsheet), OrbitPay_Security_QS.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@orbitpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Malik <priya.malik@orbitpay.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbitPay discovery — post-call recap and next steps

Monica — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. Confirming:
- We’ll send the sample prompts and a CSV of recent parser failures by EOD tomorrow (Priya will own).
- Timeline looks fine — POC doc in 3 business days is reasonable.

I attached two things to speed setup:
1) OrbitPay_SampleSchema_v1.json — a lightweight draft of RouteDecision and getQuote request/response shapes.
2) OrbitPay_Security_QS.pdf — short answers and our SOC2 point of contact.

Two clarifying items:
- For function-calls: we prefer an explicit function-call handshake (model emits a function call with name 'getQuote' and structured args). If a cached quote is used, the response should include a flag quote_source: \"cache\" or \"live\".
- On retries: we cannot accept silent population of default values — retries must surface if the model cannot produce a schema-valid response after the retry budget.

We’re excited to see the POC plan. I’ll be available for a quick sync with the SE team if needed.

—Alex
Alex Jordan
Head of Product — Payments, OrbitPay
Attachments: OrbitPay_SampleSchema_v1.json, OrbitPay_Security_QS.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OrbitPay discovery — function-call acceptance / POC ask

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding OrbitPay thread. Key asks for the POC:
- Validate the attached sample schema and propose the endpoint contract we should expose (REST + function-call handshake).
- Can we support the deterministic re-prompt + validation flow Monica described within the retry budget (recommended: 2 retries)? Any implications for token cost and latency?
- Rishi, can you prioritize a short demo script that shows: 1) model emits getQuote(function-call), 2) Redwood executes the call, 3) model returns final RouteDecision JSON that validates against the provided schema. Ideally under 250ms P95 in a dedicated sandbox.

Adding timeline: we’ll have the POC doc ready in 3 business days and request OrbitPay to spin up test credentials for sandbox.

Thanks — Monica
